findings.source_locator: After Blake snorts at Mascara-face's demand to be released
findings.why_it_matters: The deadpan aside 'The noise even sounded piggish' is a small but voice-defining comic beat; the draft converts it to 'sounding exactly like a pig,' losing the ironic understatement and the narrator's dry register.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the original: 'Blake snorted. The noise even sounded piggish.' The phrasing is distinctive and shapes the narrator's tone.

findings.source_passage: A terrible hush fell over us as he marched back to the front. The truck started forward down the gravel road. A few sniffles broke the silence.
findings.source_locator: After Blake drops the canvas and returns to the cab, before Olivia snaps 'Will you guys shut up'
findings.why_it_matters: The source's three-sentence rhythm—'terrible hush,' truck moving, sniffles—creates a specific tonal drop that marks the emotional atmosphere of the scene. The draft collapses this transition to a single brief beat, erasing the pacing and the word 'terrible hush' that carries interpretive weight about the women's collective fear.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the three-beat transition: 'A terrible hush fell over us as he marched back to the front. The truck started forward down the gravel road. A few sniffles broke the silence.'

findings.source_passage: She swept her eyes over our little group and sneered at them.

findings.why_it_matters: The small action beat of Olivia sweeping her eyes and sneering characterizes her contempt visually; the draft omits it, slightly flattening the menace of the character introduction.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the action tag back before Olivia's summary speech to preserve her physical characterization.

findings.source_passage: A flash of red blinded my vision. I screamed and lunged at the closest asshole.
findings.source_locator: Miriam's reaction when Stephanie is flung to the ground
findings.why_it_matters: 'A flash of red blinded my vision' is the narrator's kinesthetic signature for rage—it is distinctive and recurs in this type of fiction as a motif. The draft replaces it with the generic 'Heat flashed through me,' which loses both the visual/visceral specificity and the word 'asshole,' a character-voice marker.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore: 'A flash of red blinded my vision. I screamed and lunged at the closest asshole.'

summary: No high-severity signature losses; two medium findings (comic aside flattened, atmosphere-establishing transition collapsed) and two low findings (physical characterization beat dropped, rage-motif phrasing genericized) — threshold for regeneration not reached, but a revision pass should restore the flagged beats.
